title: fix(service-storage): answer an organization change at the chunk door and the progress door's expiry stamp with 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, not an outage 500
body:
Fixes #22218
Clause-②: no

The chunk door and the progress door of `@objectstack/service-storage` now answer an uploader whose active organization changed after starting an upload with the same `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` that PR #22216 gives at the commit and chunked-completion doors. They used to answer `500 INTERNAL` with the store's data-engine outage text. The progress door asks only when the session's expiry stamp is due. Which organization an upload belongs to does not change, and the tenant scope of every write is unchanged.

## Rulings carried (triage `6054616896`, verbatim)

- "Direction: the same 409 that PR #22216 gives, asked before the write"
- "⛔ No change to which organization owns an upload (#22046's ruling). ⛔ No catch-all that would hide a real engine failure."

## What changed

Only `packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts` changed in source. `metadata-store.ts` is untouched: PR #22216's `organizationOutOfWriteReach` answers both writes as it stands.

- **Chunk door** (`PUT …/upload/chunked/:uploadId/chunk/:chunkIndex`): it calls `requireStartingOrganization(writeContext, [session], 'chunk', …)` right after the resume-token check. That is before the expiry stamp, before the chunk goes to the storage backend, and before the progress write. The door writes only the session row, so only that row is asked about.
  - The resume token stays first. It is this door's proof that the caller may act on the upload, and the door has no uploader rule (#22046's ruling covers the commit, chunked-completion and progress doors). A caller without the token still gets `403 INVALID_RESUME_TOKEN` and learns nothing about organizations.
  - Before this change, a refused chunk was sent to the backend first. Its bytes landed, and only the session write after it failed.
- **Progress door** (`GET …/upload/chunked/:uploadId/progress`): the expiry decision is split out of `expireIfPastDeadline` as `expiryStampDue(session)`, and the write as `stampExpired(session, context)`. `expireIfPastDeadline` is now the composition of the two, so its behaviour at the chunk and chunked-completion doors is unchanged. The progress door computes `due` once. When the stamp is due, it calls `requireStartingOrganization(writeContext, [stored], 'progress', …)` and then stamps. The call comes after the uploader rule, as at the other doors.
- `requireStartingOrganization`, the `409` constants and the warn line are reused unchanged. The warn names the door (`chunk:` / `progress:`), the upload id, the starting organization and the active one. No new error code and no `packages/spec` change.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/22218-chunk-progress-org-change-4xx.md`, a `patch` for `@objectstack/service-storage`.

### Why the progress door asks only when the stamp is due (H3's decision)

- The question is about the reach of a write. A progress read of a live session, or of one already `expired`, writes nothing, so there is no reach to miss. It answers `200` today from any organization, and the card does not ask to change that.
- Asking on every call would turn that `200` into `409`. That narrows a published accept set (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`), against the ruled `Clause-②: no`. It would also contradict PR #22216's own wall pin, "UNCHANGED — the progress door still answers the uploader after the switch".
- `due` is computed once and drives both the question and the stamp. The question and the write therefore cannot disagree about a deadline that passes between two clock reads.
- This choice is pinned. Ablation leg C (below) removes the `due &&` guard, and the pins go red.

## Before and after, on the booted organization wall

Measured in `packages/plugins/organizations` with `bootStack`, `OrganizationsPlugin`, `StorageServicePlugin` and posture `isolated`. The uploader switches organization through the product's own `set-active` door. To put a session past its deadline, `expires_at` is moved into the past as SYSTEM, in the session's own organization.

| door | before (base `f4bed58341`) | after (`c26b15c37c`) |
|---|---|---|
| chunk, organization changed | `500 INTERNAL`, "StorageMetadataStore: sys_upload_session update failed against the data engine — the persisted upload progress is stale … Restore the data engine …", cause "Record … not found in sys_upload_session" | `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, "This upload was started in a different organization than your active one. …"; session row unchanged; switching back lands the chunk (`200`, `uploaded_chunks` 1) |
| progress past `expires_at`, organization changed | `500 INTERNAL`, the same text | `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`; the session is not stamped; switching back answers `200` `expired` and stamps it |
| chunk, same organization | `200` | `200` (control) |
| progress past `expires_at`, same organization | `200` `expired` | `200` `expired` (control) |
| progress of a live session, organization changed | `200` | `200` (unchanged) |

H1 and H2 were measured as stated. Both are throws from the scoped `UPDATE`, wrapped by `engineOp` as `StorageMetadataStoreError`. The "before" column comes from the new wall file run against the base's `storage-routes.ts`. That file was swapped in on disk inside a trap-armed script and restored to the HEAD blob afterwards. Result: "Tests 2 failed | 8 passed (10)", and the failing two are exactly the two negative pins.

## Tests

- `storage-routes.metadata-outage.test.ts`: two new blocks inside the existing #22175 block, plus one stand-in case. All use that file's existing fake engine; no new double was pinned.
  - **Chunk door (6 cases):**
    - From another organization: `409` with the code and first sentence. The backend `uploadChunk` is never called, the session row is unchanged, and the warn names `chunk:`, the upload and both organizations.
    - Asked before the expiry write: from another organization the session is not stamped, while the same organization gets `410` and the stamp.
    - Same-organization control: `200`.
    - A same-organization **real engine failure** still answers `500 INTERNAL` with "Restore the data engine".
    - An org-less session stays in reach (`200`).
    - The resume token runs first: `403 INVALID_RESUME_TOKEN`, with no mention of organizations.
  - **Progress door past its deadline (6 cases):**
    - From another organization: `409`, not stamped, and the warn names `progress:`.
    - Same-organization control: `200` `expired`, stamped.
    - A same-organization real engine failure on the stamp still answers `500` with "Restore the data engine".
    - Asked only when due: an already `expired` session answers `200` from the other organization.
    - An org-less session is stamped from any organization (`200`).
    - The ownership rule runs first: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`.
  - **Stand-in:** the engine-absent store answers both doors from any organization, as before.
- `storage-upload-organization-change.wall.test.ts`: 4 new cases. For both doors: the negative pin with switch-back, and a same-organization control.

## Ablation (from committed `c26b15c37c`)

Three legs, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode under the verify lock. Each anchor hit x1 and went to x0, and each restore was proven by the tool ("blob == HEAD (5fe0c1aed093) and `git diff HEAD` is empty"). Afterwards: anchors 1/1, markers 0, status clean. Both suites resolve the subject from `src`: the organizations vitest config aliases `@objectstack/service-storage` to `src/index.ts`, and the unit file imports `./storage-routes.js`. So no `dist` leg applies.

| leg | mutation | wall | unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | the chunk door's question removed (blob → `091b433f37f1`) | 1 red: the chunk pin, which received `500 INTERNAL` with the outage text | 3 red: `409`, expiry-first, token-then-409 |
| B | the progress door's question removed (blob → `f621826ca74d`) | 1 red: the progress pin, `500 INTERNAL` with the outage text | 1 red |
| C | the `due &&` guard removed, so the question is asked on every progress call (blob → `78b594f67293`) | 1 red: #22216's "UNCHANGED — the progress door still answers…" pin, which received `409` | 2 red: "asked only when the stamp is due" and #22216's progress-read pin |

## Acceptance notes

- **The seed helper's org-less arm was vacuous; fixed here, because the new pins depend on it.** The helper in `storage-routes.metadata-outage.test.ts` took `sessionOrganization: string | undefined = 'org_a'`, and `seed(store, undefined)` takes the default. So PR #22216's case "a session row with no organization still answers 409 when its FILE row is out of reach" seeded the session in `org_a`. It passed for that reason, not for the reason its title gives.
  - Measured here: the two new org-less cases first answered `409`, not `200`, in the first run at `3be6d508d4`.
  - The helper now takes `null` for "no organization". Each org-less case, the #22175 one included, asserts its premise (`organization_id` undefined), and all three pass.
- **Release text:** PR #22216's pending changeset (`.changeset/22175-upload-org-change-4xx.md`) lists "the progress door" under **Unchanged**. That was true of that change. This PR's changeset states the progress door's new answer for a session past its deadline, so the two entries will sit side by side in one release's CHANGELOG. Neither changeset is edited here.
